info.name: Bulb API
info.description:
On/off bulb control API for ESP32, with cron schedules.

Interactive docs: {{baseUrl}}/docs (Swagger UI).

GET /bulb is unversioned and frozen — deployed devices poll it. Every /v1/ endpoint returns a { success, data } envelope.

request.description: Unversioned, frozen shape { is_on, updated_at } polled by deployed devices. Do not change this endpoint.
Current state inside the standard envelope, with an RFC 3339 timestamp.
Set the bulb on or off via JSON body.

item.name: Schedules
item.description: Cron schedules that switch the bulb on or off. Cron is SIX fields, seconds first: 'second minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week'. Fields are read in the server's SCHEDULE_TZ (default Asia/Jakarta), so "0 0 5 * * *" means 05:00 local time — not UTC. A 5-field crontab expression is rejected with a 400.

request.description:
Create a schedule and start running it immediately.

Cron is SIX fields, seconds first: 'second minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week'. Fields are read in the server's SCHEDULE_TZ (default Asia/Jakarta), so "0 0 5 * * *" means 05:00 local time — not UTC. A 5-field crontab expression is rejected with a 400.

'action' must be "on" or "off". The cron expression is validated before anything is written, so an invalid one leaves no row behind.

This request saves the new id into {{scheduleId}} for the requests below.

exec: // Save the new schedule's id into {{scheduleId}} so the requests
// below (get / update / disable / delete) work without copy-pasting.

request.description: One schedule by id. 400 if the id is not a UUID, 404 if unknown.

Update any subset of name / cron_expr / action / enabled — omitted fields keep their current value.

The running cron job is replaced, so a new time takes effect immediately rather than at the next restart.
Stop the job without deleting the row. Send { "enabled": true } to resume it.
Delete the schedule and stop its job. Returns the row that was removed.
